title: Solutions of $a^p=a$ in a local ring of characteristic $p$
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $R$ be a local ring (a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) in which $p\cdot1_R=0$, so that $R$ is an algebra over $\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$ via $c\mapsto c\cdot1_R$. If $a\in R$ satisfies $a^p=a$, then $a=c\cdot1_R$ for exactly one $c\in\mathbf F_p$. Equivalently, the map $\mathbf F_p\to\{a\in R:a^p=a\}$, $c\mapsto c\cdot1_R$, is a bijection.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence (stalk of the kernel of $\wp$); the fact is used without proof in Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Section 0A3J (label section-artin-schreier), where the Artin–Schreier sequence is asserted to be exact

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m$ be the unique maximal ideal of $R$, let $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, and write $q:R\to\kappa$ for the quotient homomorphism. Maximality makes $\kappa$ a field. Since $p\cdot1_R=0$, also $p\cdot1_\kappa=0$. If $a^p=a$, then $q(a)^p=q(a)$ because $q$ preserves powers. By [lem-sc-field-artin-schreier-kernel] applied to $\kappa$, there is a unique $c\in\mathbf F_p$ with $q(a)=c\cdot1_\kappa=q(c\cdot1_R)$.

source.place: Tag 0A3J (section-artin-schreier), opening assertion about the kernel; residue-field reduction makes its field calculation applicable to the local ring

proof.text: Put $b=a-c\cdot1_R$. The equality of their images under $q$ gives $b\in\mathfrak m$. The binomial theorem in characteristic $p$ gives $b^p=a^p-(c\cdot1_R)^p=a-c\cdot1_R=b$: each intermediate binomial coefficient is divisible by the prime $p$, and $(c\cdot1_R)^p=c\cdot1_R$ because $c^p=c$ in $\mathbf F_p$ by [lem-sc-field-artin-schreier-kernel]. Since $p\ge2$, the ideal property yields $b^{p-1}\in\mathfrak m$, whence $1-b^{p-1}\notin\mathfrak m$ (otherwise $1$ would lie in the proper ideal $\mathfrak m$). Thus $1-b^{p-1}$ is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion]. Now $b(1-b^{p-1})=b-b^p=0$, and multiplication by the inverse of this unit gives $b=0$. Therefore $a=c\cdot1_R$.

source.place: Tag 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring), equivalence (1) and (3), for the unit criterion; Tag 0A3J (section-artin-schreier) states the kernel identification without this calculation

proof.text: Conversely, for each $c\in\mathbf F_p$, [lem-sc-field-artin-schreier-kernel] says $c^p=c$, and the canonical ring map $\mathbf F_p\to R$ preserves powers, so $(c\cdot1_R)^p=c\cdot1_R$. The map from $\mathbf F_p$ therefore lands in the stated solution set, and step 2 proves surjectivity. If $c\cdot1_R=d\cdot1_R$, applying $q$ gives $c\cdot1_\kappa=d\cdot1_\kappa$; injectivity of the map $\mathbf F_p\to\kappa$ in [lem-sc-field-artin-schreier-kernel] gives $c=d$. Hence the map is bijective.
